newsitem.title: EGYPT: EU blames Israel for hardship in Gaza, West Bank.
newsitem.headline: EU blames Israel for hardship in Gaza, West Bank.

text.p: The European Union blamed the Israeli government on Monday for some of the economic hardship in the West Bank and Gaza and said it should reconsider policies which harm the Palestinian economy.

Dick Spring of Ireland, head of a "troika" delegation of three EU foreign ministers, told a news conference they would probably raise their complaint when they meet Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy in Cairo on Tuesday.

Spring and the foreign ministers of Italy and the Netherlands, Lamberto Dini and Hans Van Mierlo, are on the last stop of a Middle East tour and will take part in the opening session of a Middle East economic conference on Tuesday.

"We feel very strongly that there are opportunities in the economic sphere which the Israeli government has not in any way been helpful to. I think it's very important these developments are allowed to go ahead as quickly as possible," said Spring.

"We're talking about the closure of the borders, the building of a port in Gaza and we're talking about access to the airfield and other measures. This...struck us very firmly from our discussions with the Palestinian Authority," he added.
"If time permits we will bring up (with Levy) every relevant issue in relation to the Middle East peace process and...the economic issues I have just mentioned," he said.

Spring and Foreign Minister Amr Moussa, who was also present, said they doubted Israel and the Palestinians would sign an agreement on Israeli redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron during the Cairo conference.
"We have no information about any ceremony in relation to the Hebron aspect of the Oslo accord," said Spring.
"It is not scheduled and there will be no ceremony or anything of the sort," added Moussa.
The visit of the "troika" ministers, whose countries are the former, current and next presidents of the European Union, helped make Cairo the focus of Middle East diplomacy on Monday.
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat arrived on Monday afternoon and U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher flew in later in the day.

Moussa said he would meet Arafat, who would then have meetings with the troika and then with Christopher. Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak saw the troika earlier on Monday and will meet some of the visiting leaders on Tuesday.
Spring said the troika would meet Christopher and said Europe wanted to cooperate in the Middle East with the United States, the dominant mediator between Israel and the Arabs.

The troika visited Syria, Jordan and the Palestinian territories, but not Israel because of their dispute with the right-wing government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over visits to the PLO headquarters in East Jerusalem.
